sections.heading: Good vs bad debt
sections.body: Debt that builds assets or income (e.g., education, affordable housing) can be acceptable. High-interest consumer debt (credit cards, unsecured loans) is costly and should be paid down first.

sections.heading: Debt-to-income (DTI)
sections.body: Keep monthly debt payments below 36% of net income. In the Philippines, banks often use 40% as a limit for housing loans. Paying more than the minimum on high-interest debt saves interest and shortens the term.
